latin: Poteris ex praecedenti conclusione aliquid intelligere de pelliceis tunicis quas sibi fecit Adam, et de pellibus quae erant in Tabernaculo.
translation: From the preceding conclusion you will be able to understand something about the tunics of skin that Adam made for himself, and about the skins that were in the Tabernacle.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch16, from Latin at farmer1998:24941
doctrine: The conclusion extends the preceding conclusion, on Zoroaster's dog as the irrational soul, to two biblical images, Adam's tunics of skin (Genesis 3:21) and the skins of the Tabernacle (Exodus 36:19), both heavily glossed in medieval exegesis (farmer1998:24972). Farmer identifies the tabernacle skins as red rams' skins forming part of the veil, which Pico's Cabalistic theses treat as a symbol of Christ, and notes the Christian tradition that the veil was torn at Christ's death, making the skins here a figure of Fall and Redemption (farmer1998:24972).
historiography: A German-language study of Pico's epistemology and Kabbalah connects this conclusion to the Temple veil (Tempelvorhang) and to two Cabalistic conclusions on the death of Christ, 11>38 and 11>46, citing a discussion by Pompeo Faracovi (kabbalah_paradigma:2121).
